Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 109, verses 1–6:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His mention and sanctified be His names: ﴿Say, "O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and the polytheists among his people, as it is related, had proposed to him that they would worship God for one year on condition that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) worship their gods for one year. So God sent down the answer to their request concerning that: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who asked you to worship their gods for a year, on condition that they worship your God for a year, ﴿O disbelievers﴾ in God, ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ of gods and idols now, ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ now.

﴿Nor am I a worshipper﴾ in what I will do in the future ﴿of what you have worshipped﴾ in the past, ﴿nor are you worshippers﴾ in what you will do in the future, ever, ﴿of what I worship﴾, I now, and in the future. This was said in this way because the address from God was to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning specific individuals among the polytheists, whom He knew would never believe, and this had been decreed for them in His prior knowledge. So He commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to dispel from them the hope they had cherished and the desire they had entertained, and to make clear that this would never happen, from him or from them, at any time. The Prophet of God (ﷺ) despaired of hoping for their belief and of their ever prospering. Thus they did not prosper or succeed, until some of them were killed by the sword at the Battle of Badr, and some died in disbelief before that.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said, and reports have come to that effect.

Mention of those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi narrated to me, saying: Abu Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that the Quraysh promised the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that they would give him wealth so that he would become the richest man in Mecca, and marry him to whatever women he wished, and provide for his lineage. They said to him: "This is yours with us, O Muhammad, and refrain from insulting our gods, and do not mention them with evil. If you do not do so, we offer you one thing, which is for you and for us, and in it is benefit for us." He said: "What is it?" They said: "You worship our gods for a year: al-Lat and al-Uzza, and we will worship your God for a year." He said: "Until I see what comes from my Lord." Then revelation came from the Preserved Tablet: ﴿Say, "O disbelievers"﴾ to the end of the surah. And God revealed: ﴿Say, "Is it other than God that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?"﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿So worship, and be among the thankful.﴾

* Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Sa'id ibn Mina, mawla of al-Bakhtari [[His Diwan: 58; Sibawayh 1: 375; Majaz al-Qur'an: 101; al-Khizanah 2: 314. This verse is said by al-Nabigha to Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari. Banu Uqaysh: they are the Banu Uqaysh ibn Ubayd. It was said: a clan of Ashja'. It was said: a tribe of Yemen whose camels are extremely skittish. It was said: they are a tribe of jinn, as they claim. Qa'qa'a means to shake something dry so that a sound is heard from it. Al-Shann: an old, worn-out waterskin. He describes Uyayna as cowardly, weak, and extremely fearful, like a camel that is very skittish when it hears the sound of a waterskin being shaken.]] said: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and Umayya ibn Khalaf met the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, come, let us worship what you worship, and you worship what we worship, and we will make you a partner in all our affairs. If what you have brought is better than what is in our hands, we will have shared in it and taken our portion of it; and if what is in our hands is better than what is in your hands, you will have shared in our affairs and taken your portion of it." So God revealed: ﴿Say, "O disbelievers"﴾ until the surah ended.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: For you is your religion, so you will never abandon it, because it has been sealed upon you and decreed that you will not be turned away from it, and that you will die upon it. And for me is my religion, which I follow, and I will never abandon it, because it has passed in the prior knowledge of God that I will not move from it to another.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the saying of God: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾: "It is for the polytheists." He said: "The Jews worship none but God and do not associate partners with Him, except that they disbelieve in some of the prophets and in what they brought from God, and they disbelieve in the Messenger of God and in what he brought from God, and they killed groups of the prophets unjustly and aggressively. He said: Except for the remnant that remained, until Nebuchadnezzar came out, and they said: 'Uzayr is the son of God.' He called upon God and they did not worship him, and they did not do as the Christians did, who said: 'The Messiah is the son of God,' and worshipped him."

Some scholars of Arabic used to say: He repeated His saying: ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ and what follows it for emphasis, as He said: ﴿Indeed, with hardship is ease. Indeed, with hardship is ease.﴾ And as in His saying: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire; then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.﴾

End of the commentary on Surah al-Kafirun.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 109, verses 1–6:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His mention and sanctified be His names: ﴿Say, "O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and the polytheists among his people, as it is related, had proposed to him that they would worship God for one year on condition that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) worship their gods for one year. So God sent down the answer to their request concerning that: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who asked you to worship their gods for a year, on condition that they worship your God for a year, ﴿O disbelievers﴾ in God, ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ of gods and idols now, ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ now.

﴿Nor am I a worshipper﴾ in what I will do in the future ﴿of what you have worshipped﴾ in the past, ﴿nor are you worshippers﴾ in what you will do in the future, ever, ﴿of what I worship﴾, I now, and in the future. This was said in this way because the address from God was to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning specific individuals among the polytheists, whom He knew would never believe, and this had been decreed for them in His prior knowledge. So He commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to dispel from them the hope they had cherished and the desire they had entertained, and to make clear that this would never happen, from him or from them, at any time. The Prophet of God (ﷺ) despaired of hoping for their belief and of their ever prospering. Thus they did not prosper or succeed, until some of them were killed by the sword at the Battle of Badr, and some died in disbelief before that.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said, and reports have come to that effect.
